title: On Thomist premises the division held even before the fall
source_text: XXX. Quin ista gratiae divinae partitio in sufficientem atque efficacem, secundum Doctorum istorum hypotheses, locum habere debuit in natura etiam integra. Etenim, ex illorum doctrina, ut creatura quaevis agat, non satis est ut habeat agendi potentiam a creatore concessam, sed praeterea necesse est ut causa prima illam ad agendum applicet atque praemoveat. Ac proinde ut creatura integra reipsa bene ageret, non solum opus habuit auxilio, quo darentur ipsi bene agendi vires; sed praeterea alio, quo Deus facultates ejus ad bene agendum efficaciter moveret ac praedeterminaret. Unde sequitur Angelos Apostatas habuisse quidem auxilium sufficiens ad perseverandum, sed ipsis defuisse auxilium efficax necessarium ut actu perseverarent: bonis autem Angelis datum esse auxilium ad perseverandum, non tantum sufficiens, sed etiam per se efficax.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. Nay that partition of divine grace into sufficient and efficacious, according to the hypotheses of these Doctors, must have had place in nature even intact. For, from their doctrine, that any creature act, it is not enough that it have the power of acting granted by the creator, but besides it is necessary that the first cause apply it to acting and premove it. And therefore that the intact creature should in reality act well, it had need not only of help, by which strengths of acting well were given to it; but besides of another, by which God should efficaciously move and predetermine its faculties to acting well. Whence it follows that the Apostate Angels had indeed sufficient help for persevering, but to them was lacking the efficacious help necessary that they should persevere in act: but to the good Angels was given help for persevering, not only sufficient, but also efficacious by itself.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXX. Indeed, on these doctors' assumptions, the division of divine grace into sufficient and efficacious must have applied even to unfallen nature. On their teaching, for any creature to act it is not enough to have the power of acting granted by the Creator; the first cause must also apply that power to acting and move it beforehand.

So for the unfallen creature actually to do good it needed not only an aid that gave it the strength to do good but also another by which God would effectively move and predetermine its faculties to do good. It follows that the apostate angels did have sufficient aid for persevering but lacked the efficacious aid required for actually persevering, while the good angels were given aid for persevering that was not only sufficient but efficacious of itself.
